title: Inference for Welfare-Maximizing Cutoffs When the Crossing Slope Vanishes
banked_reason: D0.5 achieved subfield below the field floor; the sharp inference frontier remains open and bounded D0 repairs cannot lift the tier.
gap_reasons: The confidence-set result establishes only a conservative logarithmic diameter bound, with neither log-free adaptation nor an optimality lower bound, so it does not establish a sharp inference frontier

The highly structured crossing class and absence of implemented simulations or a worked biomarker analysis limit the significance and reproducible practical evidence for a leading econometrics journal
proof_attempt_summary: The D-stage developed a row-uniform quadratic–cubic–quartic cutoff transition law and a finite-cell honest confidence set with logarithmic adaptive diameter. It resolved the Kim–Pollard source check using the author-hosted scan, then D0.5 graded the delivered result subfield, below the required field floor. A log-free adaptive inference construction or matching optimality frontier remains open and would require a new research program; two non-tier panel findings on C4 assumption economy and related-work positioning also remain.
tldr: Balanced randomization identifies the welfare of every scalar threshold rule, while the raw empirical-welfare cutoff changes law as the crossing slope vanishes and local response curves become asymmetric. The proved row-uniform approximation has quadratic, cubic, and quartic Brownian drift under the strict margin \(|q_n|\le2(1-\varepsilon)\sqrt{\kappa_nc_n}\), retains the row-specific variance, and recovers the quartic and Chernoff endpoints. The computable finite-cell multiscale value-difference set has, for every sufficiently large finite row, uniform coverage at least \(1-\alpha/n^2\) and logarithmic adaptive expected length. This conservative guarantee is not exact nominal coverage. The transition-scale Taylor expansion is asserted uniformly only for bounded \(\lambda_n\), no minimax claim or explicit variance-pair witness is asserted, and log-free adaptation over both signs of \(q_n\) remains open.
gap: Crippa (2025) and Cheng and Yang (2024) derive causal regime-parameter laws under fixed positive curvature. Fixed-order generalized Grenander theory does not cover a raw causal cutoff with jointly local linear and quadratic crossing coefficients, a quadratic--cubic--quartic triangular drift, and nonconvergent row-specific variance.
fill: A strict discriminant margin couples asymmetry to curvature, the balanced radius compactifies the admissible polynomial drifts, a two-sided martingale functional central limit theorem supplies the row-specific Brownian process, and direct localized value-difference inversion yields honest adaptive length.
